title: Ashbury Rewards Earning Rules for Completed Stays
content:
## 1. What a stay earns

A completed stay credited to an Ashbury Rewards membership earns base points and, at elite tiers, an elite bonus, posted as two separate transactions when the folio is settled. The stay earns only when the reservation's rate plan earns base points and its booking channel earns under the plan's rules for bookings made through online travel agencies and through travel agencies on the global distribution systems; the elite bonus is posted only when the plan also earns elite bonus points.

## 2. Eligible spend

Eligible spend is the sum of the folio's room lines and, when eligible incidental charges earn base points, its lines whose charge code is among the eligible incidental charge codes, less every adjustment and elite breakfast credit posted against those lines. Taxes, resort fees, parking, pet, smoking cleaning, late check-out and early departure charges never count.

## 3. Base points

Base points are the eligible spend multiplied by the base points per US dollar of the hotel's brand — the rate of Ashbury Express, Ashbury Inn & Suites, Ashbury Hotel, Ashbury Grand, Ashbury Resort & Spa or Ashbury Reserve, as the case may be — rounded down to a whole point.

## 4. Elite bonus — retired clause

> **No longer in force.** The clause "The elite bonus is the base points times the elite bonus percentage of the member's tier, rounded down; when the elite bonus applies to incidentals it is applied to all base points" is no longer in force. It is superseded by the current basis for the elite bonus of a stay. The tier's elite bonus percentage itself remains the tier's figure.

## 5. The tier of the stay

The member's tier is the tier shown on the membership when its tier effective date is on or before the stay's check-out date. When the tier took effect after the check-out date, the tier held during the stay cannot be read from the records; the base points are posted and the elite bonus is left to Ashbury Rewards member services.

## 6. Several rooms, account status and single posting

When one member holds several rooms with overlapping nights at one hotel, at most the tier's number of rooms that earn points per stay earn points. Points are posted only to a membership whose status is active. A stay earns each earning component — base points and elite bonus — at most once.

## Components posted (condition table)

| Plan earns base points and channel earns | Plan earns elite bonus points | Tier readable at check-out | Base points posted | Elite bonus posted under these rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No | — | — | No | No |
| Yes | No | — | Yes | No |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes, at elite tiers |
| Yes | Yes | No (tier took effect after check-out) | Yes | No — left to Ashbury Rewards member services |

## Worked figure (hypothetical folio)

A stay at a hotel whose brand rate is taken, for the illustration, as 10 points per US dollar, with these folio lines: room 540.00, breakfast 45.00, spa 120.00, minibar 30.00, resort fee 75.00, room tax 64.80, an adjustment of 20.00 against breakfast and an elite breakfast credit of 25.00 against breakfast. Eligible spend is 540.00 plus 45.00 plus 120.00, less 20.00 and less 25.00, which is 660.00; minibar is not an eligible incidental code, and the resort fee and tax never count. Base points are 660.00 multiplied by 10, which is 6600.

superseded_clauses: The elite bonus is the base points times the elite_bonus_pct of the member's tier, rounded down; when elite_bonus_on_incidentals is true it is applied to all base points.
